# Comparator file

A custom comparator file (`<name>.comparator.yaml`): YAML declarations the rules interpreter runs over the default comparator, sandboxed. Identity passes add correspondences; comparator rules, CEL expressions checked against declared types when the file loads, classify changes, order them into steps and add metadata. See the guide's "Write a custom comparator" and docs/design/declarative-comparators.md. The schema is published at its ID, `https://schemas.projections.githubnext.com/comparator/v0.json`; it is generated from TypeBox
definitions into [`packages/schemas/schemas/comparator/v0.json`](../../../packages/schemas/schemas/comparator/v0.json).

## Document

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$schema` | string |  | Editors: `# yaml-language-server: $schema=<url>` at the top of the file works too. |
| `format` | `"projections.comparator"` | Yes |  |
| `version` | `0` | Yes |  |
| `description` | string |  |  |
| `defaults` | object |  | Option values for options the comparison doesn't set. Every expression, functions included, reads them as `options.<name>`; an option the definition sets replaces its default. |
| `functions` | map of object |  | Named, typed expressions. A body sees its parameters, its own variables and the inputs (`before`, `after`, `lookup`, `options`, `baseline`), never its caller's variables or the file's (share option defaults through `defaults`). The call graph must be acyclic, so every evaluation terminates. |
| `checks` | array of object |  | Evaluated first, in order. The first `assert` that isn't true fails the comparison with `code` (default `invalid-options`), `path` (default `/options`) and `message`. |
| `identity` | array of any or any |  | Identity passes, in order. Each pass sees only the items earlier passes left unmatched. Entity passes all run before relationship passes. |
| `classify` | object |  | Evaluated per change, in change order, with `change`, `origin` (the identity pass that matched it, or null), `befores`, `afters`, `beforeItem`, `afterItem`, `changes`, `pairs` and `changeOf`. |
| `classify.where` | [`cel`](#cel) |  |  |
| `classify.summary` | [`cel`](#cel) |  | A string, or null to leave the summary unset. |
| `classify.annotation` | [`cel`](#cel) |  | Any JSON value, or null; available afterwards as `annotations[change.id]`. |
| `classify.variables` | [`variables`](#variables) |  |  |
| `steps` | [`cel`](#cel) or object or object |  | How the steps are made. Declarative: start from the baseline's steps (dropping changes the comparison no longer has), `add` new steps, `rank` them, then `summary`. Or `value`, one CEL expression for the whole list (the escape hatch). |
| `metadata` | object |  | Comparison metadata keys, merged over the baseline's; a null value is omitted. |
| `metadata.values` | map of [`cel`](#cel) | Yes |  |
| `metadata.variables` | [`variables`](#variables) |  |  |
| `variables` | [`variables`](#variables) |  |  |

No other properties are allowed.

## Definitions

### `identifier`

Type: string. Pattern `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`.

### `cel`

A CEL expression.

Type: string. At least 1 character.

### `variables`

Named values, evaluated once and in order, each able to use the earlier ones; expressions read them as `variables.<name>`.

Type: array of object.

### `values`

The values a variable or parameter can take. A `match` on it warns about keys outside them and values it doesn't handle.

Type: array of string or integer. At least 1 item. Items are unique.

### `type`

A declared type: `string`, `int`, `double`, `bool`, `dyn`, `list<T>`, `map<K, V>`, `optional<T>`, or one of the protocol's object types (`Extraction`, `Entity`, `Relationship`, `Item`, `Change`, `Step`, `Comparison`, `Side`, `Lookup`, `Finding`, `Classification`, `Pairs`).

Type: string. At least 1 character.
